targets.text: Nova now tells you what her browser found instead of losing it, holds a face in view while she talks and settles back to her idle wander after, answers to 'Nova' as readily as to 'Reachy', and looks up in thought while she is off browsing.
All five success-signal checks (c23) pass live on the robot on the delivered commit, with journal lines quoted in the delivery doc, and uv run pytest is green with the boundary test included.

A browse result always reaches the conversation: NovaBrowser.on_result delivery bypasses the 3 s inject throttle in nova_sonic.inject_text (a tool result the model itself asked for is not a flood) and carries its own sense class so a result parked while Nova speaks cannot be overwritten by an unclassed cue. Robot journal 2026-09-06 06:23:05, 06:24:21 and 06:24:56: all three results were 'dropped reason=throttled interval=0.0s' because NovaBrowser._execute_task emits the 'Done! Reading results...' progress inject microseconds before on_result.

A unit test calls NovaBrowser.on_result 0 ms after a progress inject and asserts the result reaches Sonic; on the robot a browse result arriving while Nova is silent is spoken within 5 s of 'Done! Reading results...', one arriving while she speaks is spoken right after the utterance, and the journal never shows a browse result with dropped reason=throttled.

Browse progress narration is rate-limited and phrased as status, not as a request: NovaBrowser emits 'Opening browser...', 'Starting a cloud browser session...' and 'Working on: ...' as separate injects inside one second (journal 06:24:21 shows two of the three dropped as throttled), so progress collapses to at most one cue per task phase, worded so a fresh Sonic session cannot read it as an instruction (issue #8's boomerang).

A unit test feeds NovaBrowser's four progress messages inside one second and asserts at most one status cue per task phase reaches Sonic; a stub Sonic session receiving that cue as its only input produces no browse tool call.

nova_browser.py's act path is not changed: act_get plus parsed_response on the AgentCore surface already produces the answer text (the dropped injects carried real answers, truncated in the log as 'Th', 'AW', 'Se'); this round fixes delivery, not the browser.
The round's diff to nova_browser.py touches progress emission, result delivery and queue_task dedupe only; _act_on_agentcore and the act_get call are unchanged.

Conversation-driven gaze lock (q1): the first USER transcript of a conversation makes the harness submit look_at_sound (the runtime's one-shot toward the last sound direction) and then lock_face; while the conversation is live, a refused lock ('no face known') is retried every few seconds until a face is seen; once held, the lock persists through Nova's replies and the listening gaps, and release_face is submitted only when the conversation fades. Conversation activity = a USER transcript or Nova speaking (Sonic 'speaking' edge through SonicSpeaker.idle); all spool calls run off Sonic's response thread.

On the robot: lock_face (or its 'no face known' refusal followed by retries) is submitted within 2 s of the first USER transcript, the lock survives at least one 10 s speech gap inside a conversation, and release_face lands within NOVA_CONVERSATION_FADE_S + 2 s of the last transcript or utterance; a unit test drives transcript -> speaking -> gap -> fade against a fake spool and asserts exactly that sequence.

The runtime's own refusal is the face-presence check: lock_face is refused 'no face known' when Sense.face_bbox is absent or older than MAX_FACE_AGE_S = 1.5 s (reachy-mini-cli reachy/behavior/face_lock.py), so the harness keeps no face belief of its own; a refusal is a quiet no-op logged at most once per utterance.
grep finds no face-presence belief in the harness; a unit test shows a refused lock_face logs one line per retry window and never blocks the caller.

The auto-hold never releases a lock the model asked for: LockState gains an owner (auto vs requested); the playback-end release fires only for a lock the harness took itself, a model-requested lock_face is left standing, and a motion/lock-released bus event still clears the belief either way.

A unit test: the model calls lock_face, then the conversation fades and no release_face is submitted; an automatic lock plus fade submits release_face; motion/lock-released clears the belief in both cases.

Aim quality is issue #22 (runtime gains YAW_GAIN 20 / PITCH_GAIN 12, 0.5 s detection cadence, a lock that steps rather than tracks) and is not fixed in this round; the hold is exactly as good as face-lock is today.
The runtime PR of this round changes no gain, cadence or TTL constant in reachy/behavior/face_lock.py, gaze.py or face_sense.py beyond select_face's preference.

Nova answers when addressed as 'Nova' or 'Reachy': the persona (config/persona/nova.md plus the harness/persona.py embedded default) states both names and that 'Reachy' often arrives as 'Richie' or 'Reach' (harness journal 06:25:50 to 06:34:35 today). Ori reports 'Nova, ...' gets nothing today and expects the Nova model to hear its own name well; the acceptance test measures the real transcription (h8).

On the robot, five cold 'Nova, how are you' requests and five 'Reachy, how are you' requests each get a spoken reply, with the heard line and the ASSISTANT line in the journal; outside any stay_silent window.

The runtime's canonical names gain 'nova' where the name is matched: reachy/speech/engagement.py and reachy/behavior/transcript_sense.py DEFAULT_NAMES, reachy/speech/name_match.py defaults, and the sleep wake phrase default, with collision-table entries for the new initial ('no', 'never', 'over', 'nova' vs 'no va'); shipped on the robot's wireless-motor-enable branch and on main via PR (q4).

reachy-mini-cli: DEFAULT_NAMES tuples and name_match defaults contain 'nova'; tests/test_name_match.py's collision table covers 'no', 'never', 'over', 'nova' vs 'no va' and 'Nova, come here' matches; the sleep wake phrase default accepts both names; the suite is green.

A think emote exists as one call: the runtime library already ships 'thoughtful' (ease into a tilted gazing-aside hold: pitch 8 up, yaw 10 aside, roll 5, 3 s default; reachy/behavior/library.py) and 'gaze-hold' (yaw 18, signed pitch 10, 5 s default); the harness publishes a 'think' alias tool, same shape as look_at_face, that runs thoughtful with a side (left or right, alternating by default) so the model can reach for it by the name it would guess.

A unit test pins that the think alias builds run_behavior name=thoughtful with the yaw sign of the chosen side and alternates sides by default; on the robot Sonic calling think produces a run_behavior thoughtful line in both journals.

While a browse is in flight the liveness looks up: NovaBrowser.on_state_change (busy / idle / error, present but unwired in harness/app.py today) drives a standing declare_goal of gaze-hold with an upward pitch and an aside yaw at 'busy', and clears it (declare_goal with no goal) at result or error; declare_goal re-admits every tick and clears in one call (reachy/behavior/intents.py 'Standing goal semantics'), and gaze-hold claims only the head channel, so antennas and body yaw keep feel-alive's sway.

A unit test drives busy -> idle and busy -> error on the posture component against a fake spool and asserts declare_goal gaze-hold then declare_goal None; on the robot, during a browse, state.json shows gaze-hold owning head while feel-alive keeps antennas and body_yaw.

+pitch is up (reachy/behavior/face_lock.py: '+pitch is up'), so thoughtful's default already looks up and the aside yaw sign picks left or right; the think posture yields to a face hold and to the result because arbitration is by (class, recency) with both behaviours stoppable: a later lock_face owns the head and the standing goal resumes on release, so the goal is cleared before the result is injected.
A unit test asserts the standing goal is cleared before the browse result is injected; on the robot the head drops from the browsing posture before the answer is spoken.

Deploy order and version: the robot's harness checkout is still spec/fast-witty-remembering-nova @ fc2178b while main holds PR #24 (19dde0c, v0.4.0), so the round starts by moving the robot to main; the PR bumps pyproject to 0.5.0 (PyPI refuses a repeat version); any runtime change goes through wireless-motor-enable (24 commits ahead of main) per the device ops notes.

Before the round's first deploy the robot's harness checkout is main; pyproject.toml carries 0.5.0 in the PR; runtime changes are on wireless-motor-enable on the robot and merged to reachy-mini-cli main.

Harness invariants hold: no reachy_mini SDK client, no new daemon paths, tests/test_harness_boundary.py stays green; each new behaviour gets a fail-open env kill switch in harness/switches.py (NOVA_FACE_HOLD, NOVA_THINK_POSTURE) named in the start-up switches line; the legacy main.py path (gestures.py 'pondering', wake_word.py Parakeet, face_recognition.py) is untouched.

tests/test_harness_boundary.py is green; the start-up switches line names NOVA_FACE_HOLD and NOVA_THINK_POSTURE; grep for gestures, wake_word or face_recognition imports under reachy_nova/harness/ is empty.

Live on the robot: (1) 'Nova, look up X' ends with Nova speaking what the browser found within 5 s of 'Done! Reading results...' and no 'dropped reason=throttled' line for a browse result; (2) saying the same request twice in one minute runs one AgentCore session; (3) speaking to Nova turns her head toward the voice, then locks it on the face for the whole exchange, replies and pauses included, and feel-alive resumes within a few seconds of the conversation fading, with lock_face / release_face lines in both journals; (4) 'Nova, how are you' from cold gets an answer, as does 'Reachy'; (5) during a browse the head is up and aside with antennas swaying, a conversation takes the head over, and the browsing posture returns when the conversation fades if the browse is still running.

Each of the five checks is run on the robot on the delivered commit and its journal lines are quoted in docs/deliveries/<date>-features-and-bugs-round-25.md; a check that fails or is not run is recorded as such, never as passed.

Issue #8 in scope (q6): NovaBrowser.queue_task drops a task whose normalised instruction matches the running or queued one within a 5-minute window and returns a typed {ok: true, queued: false, duplicate: true} so the browse tool can tell Nova she is already on it; one spoken request never opens two AgentCore sessions.

A unit test queues the same normalised instruction twice inside the window and asserts one task runs while the second returns {ok: true, queued: false, duplicate: true}; on the robot one spoken request never shows two AgentCore session starts.

Postures are layered, lowest first: wandering (the runtime's feel-alive base) < browsing-thinking (a standing declare_goal of gaze-hold up-and-aside while NovaBrowser is busy) < conversation (look_at_sound then lock_face, held until the conversation fades). One harness component owns the standing goal and the automatic lock, computes the top layer from (conversation live, browser busy) and issues only the transition intents: a conversation takes the head from browsing, browsing resumes on fade if the browse is still running, and wandering resumes when both end (q5).

A unit test drives (browser busy, conversation live) combinations and asserts the intent sequence: busy -> declare_goal gaze-hold; conversation -> lock_face with the goal left standing; fade with browser still busy -> release_face and the goal still standing; browser idle -> declare_goal None.

When several faces are in frame the runtime prefers an enrolled (recognised) face for face_bbox: reachy/behavior/face_sense.py select_face today picks the biggest face and lets recognition break only a near tie; it changes to recognised-first, biggest among equals (q2). reachy-mini-cli change on wireless-motor-enable and main.
reachy-mini-cli test: two faces in frame, the smaller one recognised, select_face returns the recognised one; equal recognition status returns the biggest.

Cold/warm attention window (q7): Nova is cold until a USER transcript names her ('nova', 'reachy', and the mishearings 'richie', 'reach', 'noah', matched with the runtime's is_name_match rules restated locally, cite-don't-import); a name opens a warm window of NOVA_ATTENTION_WINDOW_S (default 45 s, the runtime's Limits.attention_window_s) that every further USER transcript or Nova utterance renews. While cold, a Nova utterance generated in reply to a nameless transcript is dropped at the speaker exactly as a timed-quiet drop is (speaking.py's quiet gate: no playback, no gate arm, one named senselog line), while an utterance that follows a body cue or a tool result (an inject) within the same few seconds still plays. The mic feed to Sonic stays ungated so the name is always heard and barge-in keeps working. Kill switch NOVA_ATTENTION_GATE (default on).

Unit tests against a scripted Sonic: cold + nameless transcript -> the reply is dropped with one senselog line and no daemon post; 'Nova, how are you' -> played, and the next nameless transcript within the window -> played; 45 s silence -> cold again; an utterance after a pat inject while cold -> played. Live: five cold nameless sentences produce no audio, five cold 'Nova, ...' sentences all get a spoken reply.
Ori and anyone who talks to Nova at the desk, guests included; and the operator reading the harness and runtime journals to accept the round.
The live acceptance includes Ori and at least one guest speaking to Nova, and the delivery doc quotes both journals (reachy-nova-harness and reachy-runtime) for each check.

A spoken browse ends with the answer spoken, once. Talking to Nova turns her head toward the voice, then holds it on the face for the whole exchange, and she settles back to her wander afterwards. She answers to 'Nova' and to 'Reachy'. While she is browsing her head is up and aside, thinking, and a conversation takes precedence over it.
The delivery doc's Delivery Claims table maps every sentence of the after-state to a check in c23 with evidence, and marks any unverified sentence as unverified.

Browse answers are found and then silently throttled away (three of three this morning); Nova's head wanders while someone talks to her; saying 'Nova' gets nothing; browsing shows no outward sign at all.

The delivery doc quotes the before-state evidence already on file: the three throttled browse results of 2026-09-06 06:23-06:25 BST and the absence of any face or lock line in the runtime journal since 02:39 BST.

Challenge / adjacent-systems (harness/ledger.py, memory_compactor.py): a reply dropped by the attention gate is excluded from the ledger and so from the day's memory, the same way quiet-window utterances already are (Ledger's quiet-aware append) — otherwise the compactor distils lines nobody heard and the history replay tells the next session Nova said things she never said aloud.
A test appends an ASSISTANT transcript for a gate-dropped reply and asserts the ledger holds no line for it; the memory file after compaction contains nothing from a dropped reply.

Challenge / adjacent-systems (device rules.toml + default_rules.toml + arbitration.py): while the harness holds the head for browsing or conversation, the runtime's own head reflexes are kept off it — the nova-managed rule nova-face-noticed (face -> nod, 2 s, in the device overlay) and the shipped look-toward-sound (orient-to-sound, 12 s) would take the head from a stoppable gaze-hold by recency. The browsing layer inhibits orient-to-sound and nod through set_inhibition merged with the current set (tools.py's later-wins merge), the face lock already inhibits feel-alive and orient-to-sound, and nova-face-noticed is retired from the overlay (tombstoned through rules_overlay, enabled=false): a nod at every recognised face is the wrong reflex once the lock exists.

On the robot during a browse, a loud sound (rms_ratio >= 5) does not move the head off the gaze-hold; the device overlay shows nova-face-noticed enabled=false; a test asserts the browsing layer's set_inhibition carries orient-to-sound and nod merged with the prior set and restores it on exit.

Challenge / lifecycle (supervisor.py stop_event; runtime face_lock.py mind-offline release): the harness releases what it holds — on stop_event the gaze stack submits release_face (when owner is auto) and declare_goal None, and on start it submits both once (idempotent; 'not locked' is ok:true) — because the runtime's mind-offline release is inert on this device ('mind presence dropped reason=client-incompatible' at every runtime start), so a crashed harness would otherwise leave the head locked until the 1800 s max-hold.
A test drives start and stop of the gaze stack against a fake spool and asserts release_face + declare_goal None on both edges, with owner=model locks left alone on stop.

Challenge / failure-mode (dead camera, refused locks): lock_face retries inside a conversation back off 3, 6, 12 s up to 30 s, a conversation that never sees a face logs one 'no face known' summary line rather than one per retry, and a degraded spool answer (ok: null, the 1 s await timeout the flapping engine heartbeat produces) counts as unknown and is retried, never as locked.

A test with a spool that always refuses 'no face known' asserts the retry intervals 3, 6, 12, 24, 30, 30... and exactly one summary line per conversation; a test with ok: null answers asserts the belief stays unknown and the retry continues.

Challenge / concurrency (three producer threads): the gaze stack is single-writer — Sonic's response thread (transcript, speaking edge), the speaker worker (idle) and the browser worker (state) only set flags under a lock; one worker thread computes the target layer and issues spool ops serially, waiting out each 1 s await before the next, so lock, release and goal calls can never interleave or reorder.

A test fires transcript, speaking, idle and browser-state events from three threads concurrently for 2 s and asserts the fake spool saw a strictly serial, causally ordered op sequence with no interleaved lock/release pairs.

Challenge / observability (runtime reports 'available' for a camera that has produced no frame since boot): the harness names a dead camera — it samples reachy/events/sense/snapshot at about 1 Hz and after 60 s of frame_available=false logs one latched '[SENSE stage=vision source=runtime event=frames] dropped reason=no-frames' line (and one 'restored' line when frames return), and supervisor.status() carries eyes: live|dead|unknown. Without this, item 2 fails silently in exactly the way this pass found it.

A test feeds 60 s of frame_available=false snapshots and asserts one latched dropped line, then frames and one restored line; on the robot today the harness journal shows the no-frames line within 90 s of start.

Challenge / adjacent-systems (nova_sonic.py session restart and rotation): a must-deliver inject (a browse result) arriving while Sonic is between sessions — inject_text answers 'dropped-inactive' during the 1-3 s restart or rotation gap — is queued and sent with its age once the next session is listening; today it would be lost exactly like the throttled one.

A test makes inject_text answer dropped-inactive, then active, and asserts the browse result is sent once, with its age, after the session returns; on the robot a result landing during a rotation is still spoken.

Challenge / security-and-cost lens (tools.py IntentTools.execute): while cold, tool calls Sonic makes in reply to a nameless transcript are refused with the named reason 'not addressed' for the effectful tools (browse, forge, use_skill, author_rule, goto, run_behavior, declare_goal, set_mode, set_inhibition, create_rule, enroll_face, lock_face) so ambient talk cannot start an AgentCore session or move the body; read-only and quiet tools (recall_senses, stay_silent, end_silence, raise/lower/set voice, release_face) stay allowed.
A test: cold + nameless transcript followed by a browse tool call -> ToolRefused 'not addressed', no queue_task; warm -> queued; recall_senses while cold -> allowed.

Challenge / reversibility-and-ops (runtime restart 07:13 BST 2026-09-06): a runtime restart is not a camera recovery on this device — the receive pipeline fails at media acquisition with 'GStreamer pipeline error (gst-core-error-quark code=4): state change failed' and frame_available stays false (435/435, then 171/171 snapshots) while /dev/video0-1 are held by the daemon's processes; item 2's live acceptance is blocked on the runtime/daemon media path (reachy-mini-cli issue filed), and the harness side of item 2 ships behind NOVA_FACE_HOLD regardless, verified by unit tests against a fake spool until the camera returns.

The delivery doc records the camera state at acceptance time from a live snapshot sample (frame_available true or false, with the count) and cites reachy-mini-cli #176; if frames are absent, every item-2 live check is recorded as blocked, never as passed or failed.
